text: dsh-ntr 是面向 DSH Web 的 ACP 外接 Agent 插件。它在宿主侧挂载 ACP RPC 与事件流，并在浏览器会话中接入 Agent Client Protocol，将配置的本地 ACP Agent 会话呈现在 DSH 聊天界面。用户可在 NTR 模式选择 Agent 和模型、查看流式回复与工具活动，并处理 Agent 的权限请求；设置页用于管理 Agent、命令和模型选项。适合希望在 DSH 中使用本机 ACP Agent 的开发者。需要宿主环境中可启动的 ACP Agent 命令；插件没有列出必须填写的 API Key。

dsh-ntr connects ACP agents to DSH Web conversations. It adds agent and model controls, streams replies and tool activity, and presents permission requests in chat. Configure a runnable ACP agent command on the host; model service settings belong to that agent.
想把本机支持 ACP 的编程 Agent 接到 DSH 聊天里。
有没有办法在 DSH Web 里使用我已经安装的 Agent？
让 DSH 的会话能由外部 ACP Agent 驱动。
我想在聊天窗口里看到 Agent 的实时回复和工具过程。
怎么在 DSH 里切换外接 Agent 提供的模型？
Agent 需要授权时，希望能直接在当前会话里处理。
我想为不同会话选择不同的 ACP Agent。
能不能在设置页配置 Agent 启动命令并检查连接？
I want to use a local ACP coding agent inside DSH Web.
Can my DSH conversation stream replies from an external agent?
Let me choose an ACP agent and its model from the chat composer.
I need to review an agent permission request in the conversation.
dsh-ntr 的功能「Agent 管理」：设置页用于管理 ACP Agent 配置；每个 Agent 定义启动命令及可选工作目录。在 DSH Web 的 NTR 会话及设置界面中使用。
dsh-ntr 的功能「流式会话」：ACP 会话更新接入 DSH 聊天；Agent 工具活动作为原生工具卡片呈现。在 DSH Web 的 NTR 会话及设置界面中使用。
dsh-ntr 的功能「Agent 模型选择」：会话 composer 提供 Agent 模式控制和 ACP 选择菜单，可按配置显示 Agent 模型选项。在 DSH Web 的 NTR 会话及设置界面中使用。
dsh-ntr 的功能「权限请求处理」：Agent 的待处理权限请求显示在会话输入框上方，可在会话中回应。在 DSH Web 的 NTR 会话及设置界面中使用。
dsh-ntr 的功能「会话恢复状态」：界面为已释放的 Agent 会话显示状态提示和恢复入口。在 DSH Web 的 NTR 会话及设置界面中使用。
dsh-ntr 的功能「NTR 会话模式」：随包提供 ACP agent preset，将会话声明为由外接 ACP Agent 驱动。在 DSH Web 的 NTR 会话及设置界面中使用。
dsh-ntr 需要宿主机上配置可运行的 ACP Agent 命令；工作目录由会话提供，模型服务及其凭据由所选 Agent 自行配置。

dsh-ntr README · dsh-ntr：[English](./README.en.md) | 简体中文

在 [DSH（DeepSeek Harness）](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的网页/桌面端里，用你习惯的界面，直接和任意一个 **ACP agent**（CodeBuddy、Pi、Oh My Pi、Claude Code、OpenCode、Qoder 等）对话。

**DSH 提供界面，agent 提供能力。** 会话列表、输入框、侧栏、消息展示全部来自 DSH；推理、工具执行、文件读写、权限判断全部由你自己配置的那个 agent 完成，它跑在独立进程里，完全自治。这个插件只做一件事：把两边接通，并把 agent 的输出原样画到 DSH 的界面上。

> 模型选择、思考等级、工作模式都是 **agent 自己的概念**，不是 DSH 的模型目录。插件不替你换模型，也不会把 agent 的选择写进 DSH 的全局设置。

---

dsh-ntr README · NTR 是什么：**NTR = Negotiated Target Routing（协商式目标路由）**。

一句话：你的宿主 Agent 作为 ACP 客户端，和目标 Agent 协商能力与权限，把这一轮任务交给它执行。

---

dsh-ntr README · 安装：本插件是一个 DSH **bundle**：`package.json` 的 `dsh.bundle.patch` 声明了随包分发的两层补丁——插件本体的 `cordis.patch.yml`，与 NTR 模式 preset 的 `presets/acp/acp.patch.yml`。用 `dsh plugin` 安装后，包会加入 profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles`，补丁层**自动生效**，无需手动编辑任何配置文件。

dsh-ntr README · 方式一：从官方界面安装：打开 DSH 侧边栏的**插件**页，点**添加插件**，输入 `dsh-ntr`，点安装。装完刷新页面即可使用。

> DSH 的 npm 渠道有 24 小时防范期：刚发布的版本 24 小时内不算「最新版」，只输 `dsh-ntr` 装到的可能还是旧版。想马上用新版，把版本号一起写上，例如 `dsh-ntr@0.1.5`；不急的话，等防范期过去再照常安装或升级。
section: 方式一：从官方界面安装

text:
dsh-ntr README · 方式二：从 npm registry 安装：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-ntr@latest
```

升级重跑同一条命令即可。

> `add` 时**务必带 `@latest`**：不带的话包管理器会一直复用首次写入的版本号，之后连 `update` 也升不上去。
section: 方式二：从 npm registry 安装

text:
dsh-ntr README · 方式三：经 [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) 插件市场安装：先装市场本体：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dshmarket
```

重启 `dsh web`，打开**插件**页：dsh 0.2.1 起市场是「已安装」旁边的**插件市场**标签页；更早的版本在**设置 → 插件市场**。搜索 `dsh-ntr`，确认来源后一键安装，装完刷新页面即可使用；之后的更新检查与升级也在市场里完成。官方 DSH 桌面 App 自带这个市场，直接在 App 的**插件**页里搜索安装即可。

> 市场的插件清单来自 [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) 精选目录，每天自动刷新。若搜索结果里暂时没有 `dsh-ntr`，用方式二从 npm 安装，不影响使用。
section: 方式三：经 [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) 插件市场安装

text:
dsh-ntr README · 方式四：从源码安装：需要 Node.js ≥ 22.12.0。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/GDWhisper/dsh-ntr.git
cd dsh-ntr
npm install        # 安装构建依赖（typescript 等）
npm run build      # 编译宿主 TS 与浏览器 Bundle 到 lib/（构建产物不入库，此步必须执行）

之后升级：`git pull` → `npm run build` → 重启 `dsh web`。`add .` 以 `link:` 方式安装，重建后重启即生效，不需要重新 add。

> 从源码安装切到 npm / 市场版前，先在插件管理器里卸载旧版，并删掉 profile 里的 `node_modules/dsh-ntr`。pnpm 的 hoisted 布局会把 `link:` 目标里的 `node_modules` 留在包目录内，旧依赖会遮蔽新装的 SDK，典型报错见「常见问题」里的 `EPERM ... zod`。

dsh-ntr README · 方式四：从源码安装：> `dsh plugin` 是 pnpm 转发器，`--profile <name>` 必填；`add .` 会把当前目录以 `link:` 方式装进 profile。官方桌面 App 的 profile 由它自己的插件管理器掌管，不要对着它的 profile 跑命令行。

---

dsh-ntr README · 你需要什么：1. 一个已经装好的 DSH（Web 或桌面版）。
2. 至少一个支持 ACP 协议的 agent，用它的终端版本（CLI / TUI）即可。例如 Qoder CLI（`qodercli`）、CodeBuddy Code（`codebuddy`）、Claude Code、OpenCode——插件内置了这些常见预设；其他 agent 只要能以类似 `xxx --acp` 的方式从命令行启动，也可以直接填。

dsh-ntr README · 三步接入：1. 打开 **设置 → NTR**。
2. 在「Agent 列表」里选一个预设一键填入，或点「从零新建自定义 Agent」手填启动命令。
3. 点「测试」。成功会显示 agent 的名字和握手耗时；失败会显示可操作的错误和 stderr 尾部。

保存后，这个 agent 就出现在输入框行尾的 NTR 底座里。

dsh-ntr README · 开始对话：1. 新建一个会话，在模式选择里选「**NTR 模式**」。
2. 在输入框行尾的 NTR 底座里选一个 agent。
3. 直接说话。

agent 的回复和思考显示在主聊天区。工具活动按发生顺序插在它们中间：一行 `🛠️ **工具名** · 参数`，输出跟一个代码块。想看完整的工具输出、计划和 diff，切到对话头部的 **NTR** 标签页。

---

dsh-ntr README · NTR 底座（输入框行尾）：点一下，选哪个 agent 服务这条会话。这个菜单里只有 agent 列表——一个控件一件事。agent 自己的模型和思考等级是同一行里各自独立的芯片，各开各的菜单；如果 agent 还发布了额外配置项（温度、供应商开关等），模型芯片左边会多一个「高级」底座，点开逐项设置。首轮之前 agent 底座固定在行尾最右侧；锁定后它退场，模型和思考等级接管右端。那些清单由 agent 自己上报，不是你熟悉的 DSH 模型列表。

底座只出现在 **NTR 模式**的会话里。普通会话里看到的是 DSH 原生的模型选择器。

**一个会话一个 agent。** 首条消息发出前，底座一直在，你可以先选好、也可以反悔改选。首轮**开始**时会话就**锁定**在这个 agent 上：底座粉碎，名字变成**输入框卡片上边缘的小挂牌**（`NTR · <agent>`，骑在顶边上），挂牌只显示、不能点击——换 agent 请新建会话。模型、思考等级和「高级」芯片留在原位，它们属于同一个 agent，不涉及上下文迁移。如果首轮还没产生任何可见输出就失败/取消，锁定会自动回滚，底座回来，可以直接重选。

dsh-ntr README · `/` 命令属于 agent：在 NTR 会话里输入 `/`，弹出的是 **agent 自己的命令清单**——它通过 ACP 声明的那些（例如 `compact`、`session`、`model`），不是 DSH 的命令。选中一项只是把命令名填进输入框；回车后整行原样发给 agent，由它执行。清单在**第一条消息之前**就能用：宿主记住了这个 agent 上次会话声明的命令（从没跑过的 agent 要等第一轮之后才有）。

DSH 自己的 `/model`、`/permission`、`/export` 等在这一模式下**不会**被宿主截走：同名命令也交给 agent，宿主命令菜单与技能补全不会出现。普通会话的斜杠行为完全不变。

dsh-ntr README · 审批与 agent 自己的权限模式：agent 要动敏感的东西时会问你。询问卡出现在对话里、聊天输入框上方（插件自己的卡片），选项就是 agent 给的那些，你点哪个它照着做；设置页的「待处理权限请求」是跨会话镜像，对话没打开时在那里回答。

每个 agent 问法不一样：有的给一组选项，有的只给允许/拒绝，有的会附上它要执行的具体命令。插件把这些原样呈现给你，不预先替你决定。

**权限模式由 agent 自己定义。** 每个 agent 在输入框工具行给出它自己的模式清单（例如 `Always Ask`、`Accept Edits`、`Plan`、`Bypass Permissions`），选项文字就是 agent 下发的原文。你切换模式，agent 就按新模式决定什么时候来问你。插件不另设一套权限档，也不替你翻译这些模式名。

> **注意**：DSH 自己的「访问模式」（只读 / 工作区写入 / 完全权限）管不到外部 agent。那个 agent 在自己的进程里，DSH 的文件沙箱对它没有作用力。真正生效的是 agent 自己的权限模式，以及它向你发起的那些审批。
section: 审批与 agent 自己的权限模式

text:
dsh-ntr README · NTR 标签页：对话头部的 **NTR** 标签页显示 agent 的原始流：

- 计划和待办清单
- 每次工具调用的名称、状态、输出（默认折叠，点开看全部）
- 代码改动的 unified diff，带 `+N -M` 行数统计
- 用量读数

这个标签页是只读的：它不发消息、不取消任务、不启动进程。实时跟随，不需要手动刷新。

**主聊天区和 NTR 标签页的分工**：人和 agent 的对话在主聊天区，工具活动也按时间顺序内联在那里；NTR 标签页放主聊天区装不下的东西——计划、完整输出、diff、用量。

dsh-ntr README · 设置 → NTR：- **已接入的 NTR 智能体**：每个 agent 一行，标着进程状态。点开「展开配置与模型」看全部细节。
- **`★ 默认`**：新建 NTR 会话默认用哪个 agent。
- **每张 agent 卡片**：显示名、启动命令、npm 包名、环境变量、工作目录，全部直接摆在你面前，没有藏起来的默认值。
- **启动命令是一整行**：程序加参数，例如 `codebuddy --acp`。含空格的路径用引号包住。输入框下方会实时显示插件解析出的「程序 / 参数」。
- **测试按钮**：用当前表单里的值拉起一个一次性进程做握手，不保存、不注册。适合在改配置前先验证。
- **工作区目录**：agent 在哪个目录里干活。
- **对话中可见的模型**：agent 能报几百个模型时，这里挑你想在模型芯片菜单里看到的。没勾的仍然可用，只是不列出来。

dsh-ntr README · 你的工作区：在对话里起的 NTR 会话，工作目录就是你在这个 DSH 会话里选中的那个目录（侧栏点的那个）。对端 agent 的读文件、搜索、执行命令都在那里，它自己的进程也从那里启动。

有一类 agent 在进程启动那一刻就把工作区定死了，只改会话参数它不听。插件在它没有活动会话时会把它搬到新目录；有会话在进行时就保持原进程，不打断你的对话。

---

dsh-ntr README · 常见问题：**会被平台风控吗？会封号吗？是反代吗？**

不会，也不是反代。dsh-ntr 与 agent 之间的通信走 ACP——这是 agent 官方支持的协议入口。插件只负责启动你本地的 agent 进程并和它对话，全程不接触平台 API、不转发任何请求。模型调用由 agent 自己完成，跟你在终端里直接用它没有区别。在 NTR 提供的能力范围内合理使用，是官方允许的做法，不会因此封号。

**为什么选完 agent 之后，输入框里没看到 DSH 的模型选择器？**

那是设计如此。NTR 会话里，模型是 agent 自己的概念，所以那个位置换成了 NTR 底座。切回普通模式的会话，原生选择器就回来了。

**为什么首轮开始后，输入框行尾不显示 agent 名字了？**

dsh-ntr README · 常见问题：一个会话一个 agent。首轮之前底座留着让你改选；首轮一开始，会话就锁在这个 agent 上，名字变成挂在输入框卡片上边缘的 `NTR · <agent>` 只读小挂牌。换 agent 会丢掉它这边的上下文，所以确认锁定后只能新建会话。模型、思考等级和高级配置芯片不受影响。首轮没有任何可见输出就失败/取消时，锁定会回滚，底座回来。

**锁定后想换 agent 怎么办？**

新建一个会话重新选。已锁定的会话不会接受 `session/chat-bind` 的改绑（宿主返回 `agent_locked`），这是刻意的：新 agent 没有这段对话的上下文，假装切换只会得到一段失忆的对话。首轮没有产生任何可见输出就失败的情况例外：锁定会自动回滚，可以直接重选。

**顶部看不到 NTR 标签页？**

每条会话都有这个标签页。这条会话还没绑过 agent 时，它是空的，会提示你去选一个。先在模式选择里选「NTR 模式」，再在 NTR 底座里选一个 agent。

**agent 卡住不动了？**

dsh-ntr README · 常见问题：可以放心点停止。插件会取消这一轮，并在 agent 不理会取消时强制收尾，会话不会永久卡住。agent 自己长时间无动静时，卡住的那一轮也会被收口（见 AGENTS.md 约束 23）：声明了 `session/load` 的 agent，下一次发送会自动重启并恢复会话；没声明的会被重置，上下文丢失。卡的若是这条会话的首轮、且什么都没输出，锁定会回滚、该轮作废，下一条消息直接新建会话。agent 进程崩溃同理——支持恢复的会自动拉起并回放历史，不支持的要新建会话。

**agent 只回了一个空气泡？**

一部分 agent 会把上游失败（认证、计费、配额）当成「正常结束」。插件检测到这种情况时会补一条告警，不让失败静默。

**agent 没反应，也没报错？**

看设置页的测试按钮。它会在宿主侧跑一次完整的握手，把真正的错误（包括 stderr 尾部）显示出来。

**模型列表太长或太短？**

模型芯片的菜单没有搜索框，所以模型是**按需勾选**的。去设置页那张卡片里勾你想看的。不勾就没有那些条目，避免几百个模型刷屏。

**为什么 NTR 标签页里没有我发的消息？**

dsh-ntr README · 常见问题：那个标签页只显示 agent 的原始流（它的计划、完整工具输出、diff、用量）。你和它的对话在主聊天区，工具活动按发生顺序内联在对话里。

**为什么输入框里多了一个下拉，里面的选项我没见过？**

那是 agent 自己的权限模式，选项文字由它下发。每个 agent 的叫法不一样，插件照原样列出。它管的是 agent 什么时候来问你，与 DSH 的「访问模式」无关。

**导入了 agent，但它的权限模式和别的 agent 不一样？**

正常。模式清单由每个 agent 自己声明（`session/set_mode` 下发），插件照原样列出，不统一翻译、也不补默认值。想改叫法要在 agent 自己的配置里改。

**从源码安装切到 npm / 市场版后，启用时报 `EPERM ... zod`？**

dsh-ntr README · 常见问题：这是旧依赖残留，不是插件缺文件：错误路径里会出现 `node_modules/dsh-ntr/node_modules/.pnpm/...`。源码安装用 `link:` 指向你的仓库；pnpm 的 hoisted 布局在切到 registry 版时会把包目录换成真实文件，但会留下链接目标里的 `node_modules`。这份旧树（旧版 `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` 及其失效的 `zod` 软链）会遮蔽新装的依赖，DSH 导入时 stat 到坏链就报 `EPERM`。处理：在插件管理器里卸载 `dsh-ntr`，删除 `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-ntr`（或只删它下面的 `node_modules`），再重装并重启。桌面 App 的 profile 请直接在 App 的插件页卸载/重装，不要用命令行。

**NTR 会话里出现 `Error: unknown tool "xxx"`，紧跟一行「已添加工具：xxx」，是什么？**

dsh-ntr README · 常见问题：这是宿主给工具卡补执行记录时的显示层噪音，不是 agent 的工具调用失败。

NTR 会话里，agent 的工具在它自己的进程里跑。宿主只收到通知。宿主仍要把这张卡执行一次，因为执行记录就是卡片本身。这个工具名在宿主侧没有定义，guard 就在执行阶段注册一个虚拟工具。虚拟工具用桥记下的真实输出作答。

但宿主这一步能执行哪些工具，在请求发出前就定好了。虚拟工具在执行阶段才注册，进不了这一步。所以这个工具名第一次出现时，执行记录是 `unknown tool`。下一次组装请求时工具清单多了一项，宿主写一行「已添加工具」。

影响：每个会话里每个工具名只有第一次这样。回合不中断，agent 不受影响。那张卡看不到镜像输出，真实输出在 NTR 标签页里。

dsh-ntr README · 它能做什么（能力清单）：- **任意 ACP agent**：内置常见预设，也可以接入任何支持 stdio 的 ACP agent。自定义 agent 带「自定义」徽标。
- **多会话隔离**：多个会话可以同时跟不同 agent 对话，各自独立。
- **流式展示**：用户消息、agent 回复、思考过程、工具执行、任务计划都是流式的。
- **工具活动内联**：工具调用按发生顺序插进主聊天区，思考和回答分列它两侧，不分层。
- **真实权限**：agent 的权限模式原样列出，它的每次权限询问也原样呈现，你答什么它收到什么。
- **斜杠命令归 agent**：NTR 会话里 `/` 弹出的是 agent 自己声明的命令；DSH 的同名命令不会截走你的输入。
- **断线重连**：浏览器刷新或断网后，历史按序补齐。agent 进程崩了，声明了 `session/load` 的会在下次发消息时自动恢复。
- **空闲释放**：没有活动的 agent 进程会在空闲一段时候后自动退出，不占内存；空闲会话被挂起成可恢复状态，下一条消息经 `session/load` 恢复（只对声明了 `session/load` 的 agent 成立；没声明的仍要求没有活会话才释放进程）。窗口在设置页「进程管理」里调（1-60 分钟，默认 30 分钟），单个智能体可在其「高级」里单独覆盖。
- **Windows 可用**：npm 全局安装的 agent 在 Windows 上也能正常启动和回收，不会残留后台进程。

dsh-ntr README · 实现要点：以下每条都对应一处真实故障，改代码前先读对应文档。浏览器半区经 `/acp` RPC 与 `/api/acp/stream` SSE 和宿主半区通信；宿主半区每会话一个 `AgentBridge`，经 stdio JSON-RPC 驱动 agent 子进程。

代码位置：`src/index.ts`（插件入口）· `src/protocol.ts`（共享类型）· `src/impl.ts`（纯宿主逻辑）· `src/bridge.ts`（子进程通信桥）· `src/client/`（React 扩展）· `presets/acp/`（NTR 模式声明）· `~/.dsh/dsh-ntr/`（运行时落盘）。

dsh-ntr README · 实现要点：- **DSH 只出显示层**：插件不写全局默认模型，不接管宿主的模型目录，也不让 ACP 模型出现在 DSH 原生选择器里；唯一的模型层写入是 guard 用 `agent.model.select()` 把会话绑定记成该会话的模型选择（宿主 0.2.2+ 在 step preparation 前固定路由）。
- **工作区即侧栏路径**：侧栏点开的目录必须成为 `session/new` 的 cwd **和** agent 子进程自己的 cwd。有一条 agent（codebuddy）在进程启动那一刻就定死工作区。
- **NTR 模式 = agent preset**：由 `presets/acp/acp.patch.yml` 随包声明，不挂工具、不注入项目指令、不做 compaction，让模型可见的表面完全属于对端 agent。
- **转发严格等于用户文本**：按 `source.kind === 'user'` 挑消息，不转发标题生成、compaction 这类辅助调用，也不拼任何边界叙述。
- **逐步切分 = 原生交错的工具卡**：一个 ACP turn 按工具活动切成多个宿主 step——段以 `tool-call` 卡收尾即结束本次 stream，宿主落定消息、执行卡（真实输出经 guard 虚拟工具应答）、续跑下一步；续跑段续读同一个仍在飞的 `session/prompt`，绝不新发 prompt。卡片因此夹在两个 assistant 节点之间，与原生多步对话一致。
- **绑定必须接到请求路径上**：guard 在唤醒驱动前用 `agent.model.select()` 把绑定记成会话的模型选择（`acp/<agent>`），adapter 再做一次复查；老宿主（无 `agent.model`）才用 `agent/request` waterfall（`prepend: true`）改写请求。
- **权限模式与审批是两层，都以 agent 为准**：`composer-mode.tsx` 的控件只渲染 agent 经 `session/set_mode` 下发的 `availableModes`，不写可见标签、不翻译选项名；`session/request_permission` 原样映射给用户。插件没有自己的权限开关：agent 问了就一定到人面前。早先那套由宿主替 agent 裁定的端口语义（`decidePermission`、fs 写栅栏）已删除，见 `docs/acp-convergence.md` §2.3。
- **跨平台路径**：`impl.ts` 不能 import `node:path`，绝对路径判定与 containment 全部手写，Windows 与 UNC

dsh-ntr README · dsh-ntr：English | [简体中文](./README.md)

Chat with any **ACP agent** (CodeBuddy, Pi, Oh My Pi, Claude Code, OpenCode, Qoder, …) right inside the web/desktop app of [DSH (DeepSeek Harness)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), using the interface you already know.

dsh-ntr README · dsh-ntr：**DSH provides the interface; the agent provides the capability.** The conversation list, composer, side panel, and message rendering all come from DSH; reasoning, tool execution, file access, and permission decisions all belong to the agent you configured — it runs in its own process, fully autonomous. This plugin does exactly one thing: wire the two sides together, and render the agent's output faithfully in DSH's UI.

dsh-ntr README · dsh-ntr：> Model selection, thinking level, and work modes are **the agent's own concepts**, not DSH's model catalog. The plugin never swaps models for you, and never writes the agent's choices into DSH's global settings.

dsh-ntr README · What is NTR：**NTR = Negotiated Target Routing.**

In one sentence: your host agent acts as an ACP client, negotiates capabilities and permissions with a target agent, and hands the turn over to it.

dsh-ntr README · Installation：This plugin is a DSH **bundle**: `package.json`'s `dsh.bundle.patch` declares the two patches shipped with the package — the plugin's own `cordis.patch.yml`, and the NTR-mode preset at `presets/acp/acp.patch.yml`. After `dsh plugin` installs it, the package joins the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` and the patch layers take effect **automatically** — no config file needs editing by hand.

dsh-ntr README · Option 1: from the official UI：Open the **Plugins** page in DSH's sidebar, click **Add plugin**, enter `dsh-ntr`, and click install. Refresh the page and it's ready to use.

> DSH keeps a 24-hour safety window on the npm channel: a version published within it won't be picked as the latest, so entering plain `dsh-ntr` may install the previous release. To get the new version right away, include the explicit version in the box, e.g. `dsh-ntr@0.1.5`; otherwise wait out the window and install or upgrade as usual.

dsh-ntr README · Option 2: from the npm registry：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-ntr@latest
```

Run the same command again to upgrade.

> **Always pass `@latest`**: without it the package manager keeps reusing the version it wrote the first time, and `update` won't get you off it afterwards.

dsh-ntr README · Option 3: via the [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) plugin market：First install the market itself:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dshmarket
```

dsh-ntr README · Option 3: via the [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) plugin market：Restart `dsh web` and open the **Plugins** page: on dsh 0.2.1+ the market is the **Plugin Market** tab next to **Installed**; on older hosts it lives under **Settings → Plugin Market**. Search for `dsh-ntr`, confirm the source, and install in one click — refresh the page and it's live; update checks and upgrades afterwards also happen in the market. The official DSH Desktop app ships with this market preset, so just search and install from the app's **Plugins** page.

dsh-ntr README · Option 3: via the [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) plugin market：> The market's catalog comes from the curated [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) registry and refreshes daily. If `dsh-ntr` doesn't show up in search yet, install it from npm with Option 2 — nothing is lost.

dsh-ntr README · Option 4: from source：Requires Node.js ≥ 22.12.0.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/GDWhisper/dsh-ntr.git
cd dsh-ntr
npm install        # build dependencies (typescript, …)
npm run build      # compile host TS + browser bundle into lib/ (build output is not committed — this step is required)

To upgrade later: `git pull` → `npm run build` → restart `dsh web`. `add .` installs the directory as `link:`, so a rebuild plus a restart picks up the changes — no re-add needed.

dsh-ntr README · Option 4: from source：> Before switching from the source install to the npm/market build, uninstall the old version and delete `node_modules/dsh-ntr` from the profile. pnpm's hoisted layout leaves the linked checkout's `node_modules` inside the package directory, and the stale dependencies shadow the newly installed SDK — see the `EPERM ... zod` entry in the FAQ.

dsh-ntr README · What you need：1. A working DSH install (web or desktop).
2. At least one ACP-capable agent, using its terminal build (CLI / TUI). For example Qoder CLI (`qodercli`), CodeBuddy Code (`codebuddy`), Claude Code, or OpenCode — presets for these ship with the plugin; any other agent that starts from the command line in the same `xxx --acp` style can be filled in directly.

dsh-ntr README · Three steps：1. Open **Settings → NTR**.
2. Pick a preset from the agent list to fill it in, or click "Create a custom agent from scratch" and type the launch command yourself.
3. Click **Test**. Success shows the agent's name and the handshake latency; failure shows an actionable error plus the tail of stderr.

After saving, the agent shows up in the NTR base at the end of the composer.

dsh-ntr README · Start talking：1. Create a conversation and pick **NTR mode** in the mode selector.
2. Pick an agent in the NTR base at the end of the composer.
3. Just talk.

The agent's replies and thinking appear in the main chat. Tool activity is interleaved in order: a line of `🛠️ **tool** · args`, with the output in a code block below. For full tool outputs, plans, and diffs, switch to the **NTR** tab in the conversation header.

dsh-ntr README · NTR base (end of the composer)：Click it to choose which agent serves this conversation. The menu lists only agents — one control, one job. The agent's own model and thinking level are separate chips on the same row, each with its own menu; if the agent also publishes extra config options (temperature, provider toggles, …), an **Advanced** base appears to the left of the model chip, where you set them one by one. Before the first turn, the agent base sits pinned at the far right; once locked, it retires and model/thinking take over the right end. Those lists are reported by the agent itself — they are not your familiar DSH model list.
dsh-ntr README · NTR base (end of the composer)：The base appears only in **NTR-mode** conversations. Normal conversations show DSH's native model selector.

dsh-ntr README · NTR base (end of the composer)：**One conversation, one agent.** Until the first message is sent, the base stays put: pick, or change your mind freely. The moment the first turn **starts**, the conversation **locks** to that agent: the base collapses, and the name becomes a **small tag on the top edge of the composer card** (`NTR · <agent>`, straddling the edge) — display-only, not clickable. To switch agents, start a new conversation. The model, thinking-level, and Advanced chips stay in place; they belong to the same agent, so no context moves. If the first turn fails or is cancelled before producing any visible output, the lock rolls back automatically and the base returns for another pick.

dsh-ntr README · `/` commands belong to the agent：Type `/` in an NTR conversation and what pops up is **the agent's own command list** — the ones it declares over ACP (e.g. `compact`, `session`, `model`), not DSH's. Selecting one just inserts the command name into the composer; pressing Enter sends the whole line to the agent as-is, and it executes it. The list works **before the first message**: the host remembers the commands this agent declared in its last session (an agent that has never run has to wait until after the first turn).

dsh-ntr README · `/` commands belong to the agent：DSH's own `/model`, `/permission`, `/export`, etc. are **not** intercepted by the host in this mode: same-named commands go to the agent too, and the host's command menu and skill completions never appear. Slash behavior in normal conversations is unchanged.

dsh-ntr README · Approvals and the agent's own permission modes：When the agent wants to touch something sensitive, it asks you. The ask appears in the conversation on a card just above the composer (the plugin's own card); the options are exactly the agent's, and what you click is what it receives. The Settings page's "Pending Permission Requests" card is the cross-session mirror — answer there when the conversation isn't open.

text: dsh-ntr README · Approvals and the agent's own permission modes：Every agent asks differently: some offer a set of options, some only allow/deny, some attach the exact command they are about to run. The plugin presents these as-is, and never pre-decides for you.

text: dsh-ntr README · Approvals and the agent's own permission modes：**Permission modes are defined by the agent.** Each agent puts its own mode list (e.g. `Always Ask`, `Accept Edits`, `Plan`, `Bypass Permissions`) in the composer's tool row; the option text is exactly what the agent sent. Switch a mode, and the agent decides accordingly when to ask you. The plugin adds no permission tier of its own, and doesn't translate mode names.

The agent lives in its own process; DSH's file sandbox can't reach it. What actually applies is the agent's own permission mode, plus the approvals it sends you.

dsh-ntr README · NTR tab：The **NTR** tab in the conversation header shows the agent's raw stream:

- Plans and todo lists
- Every tool call's name, status, and output (collapsed by default; click to expand)
- Unified diffs of code changes, with `+N -M` line counts
- Usage readouts

The tab is read-only: it sends no messages, cancels no tasks, launches no processes. It follows live — no manual refresh.

dsh-ntr README · NTR tab：**Division of labor between the main chat and the NTR tab**: your conversation with the agent lives in the main chat, and tool activity is inlined there in time order; the NTR tab holds what the main chat can't — plans, full outputs, diffs, usage.

dsh-ntr README · Settings → NTR：- **Connected NTR agents**: one row per agent, with process status. Click "Expand config & models" for the full detail.
- **`★ Default`**: which agent new NTR conversations use by default.
- **Each agent card**: display name, launch command, npm package, environment variables, working directory — all in plain sight, no hidden defaults.
- **The launch command is one line**: program plus arguments, e.g. `codebuddy --acp`. Quote paths that contain spaces. Below the input, the plugin live-shows the program/arguments it parsed.
- **Test button**: launches a one-shot process with the current form values to do a handshake — nothing saved, nothing registered. Good for validating before you commit a config change.
- **Workspace directory**: the directory the agent works in.
- **Models visible in conversations**: when an agent reports hundreds of models, check here which ones appear in the model chip's menu. Unchecked ones still work; they're just not listed.

dsh-ntr README · Your workspace：An NTR conversation started in chat uses the directory you selected in this DSH session (the one you clicked in the side panel) as its working directory. The agent's file reads, searches, and command execution all happen there; its process is also launched from there.

dsh-ntr README · Your workspace：One class of agents pins the workspace the moment the process starts, and ignores session-parameter changes afterwards. The plugin relocates such an agent to the new directory when it has no active conversations; while conversations are live, it keeps the original process and doesn't interrupt you.

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：**Will the platform risk-control me? Will I get banned? Is this a reverse proxy?**

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：No, and it isn't a reverse proxy. dsh-ntr talks to agents over ACP — the officially supported protocol entry point of those agents. The plugin only launches your local agent process and talks to it; it never touches platform APIs and forwards no requests. Model calls are made by the agent itself, no different from you using it directly in a terminal. Reasonable use within what NTR provides is officially allowed, and won't get you banned.

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：**Why is DSH's model selector gone from the composer after I pick an agent?**

By design. In NTR conversations, models are the agent's own concept, so that spot becomes the NTR base. Switch back to a normal-mode conversation, and the native selector returns.

**Why does the agent name at the composer's end disappear once the first turn starts?**

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：One conversation, one agent. Before the first turn, the base stays so you can change your pick; the moment the first turn starts, the conversation locks to that agent, and the name becomes the read-only `NTR · <agent>` tag on the top edge of the composer card. Switching agents would lose this side's context, so once locked, you must start a new conversation. The model, thinking-level, and advanced-config chips are unaffected. If the first turn fails or is cancelled with no visible output, the lock rolls back and the base returns.

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：**How do I switch agents after locking?**

Start a new conversation and pick again. A locked conversation refuses rebinding via `session/chat-bind` (the host returns `agent_locked`) — deliberately: the new agent has no context of this conversation, and a fake switch would only yield an amnesiac chat. One exception: if the first turn failed without producing any visible output, the lock auto-rolls-back, and you can re-pick directly.

**Can't see the NTR tab at the top?**

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：Every conversation has this tab. If the conversation has never been bound to an agent, it's empty and prompts you to pick one. First select "NTR mode" in the mode picker, then pick an agent in the NTR base.

**Agent stuck?**

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：Click Stop without worry. The plugin cancels the turn, and force-finalizes it if the agent ignores the cancel — a conversation never hangs forever. A turn the agent goes silent in is finalized too (see constraint 23 in AGENTS.md): with `session/load` the next send restarts the agent and resumes the session; without it the session is reset and its context is lost. If that was the conversation's first turn and it produced nothing, the agent lock rolls back and the next send starts a new session. A crashed agent process behaves the same way — one that supports resume comes back with its history on the next message.

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：**Agent replied with an empty bubble?**

Some agents treat upstream failures (auth, billing, quota) as "normal completion". When the plugin detects this, it appends a warning instead of letting the failure pass silently.

**Agent unresponsive, and no error either?**

Check the Test button in Settings. It runs a full handshake on the host side and surfaces the real error (including the tail of stderr).

**Model list too long or too short?**

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：The model chip's menu has no search box, so models are **opt-in**. Check the ones you want on that settings card. Unchecked ones simply don't appear, sparing you a wall of hundreds of models.

**Why don't my messages appear in the NTR tab?**

That tab shows only the agent's raw stream (its plans, full tool outputs, diffs, usage). Your conversation with it lives in the main chat, with tool activity inlined there in order.

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：**Why is there an extra dropdown in the composer, with options I've never seen?**

That's the agent's own permission mode; the option text comes straight from it. Each agent names them differently, and the plugin lists them verbatim. It governs when the agent asks you — unrelated to DSH's "Access mode".

**Imported an agent, and its permission modes differ from other agents'?**

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：Normal. Mode lists are declared by each agent itself (sent via `session/set_mode`); the plugin lists them verbatim — no unified translation, no defaults filled in. To change the wording, edit the agent's own config.

**Activation fails with `EPERM ... zod` after switching from the source install to npm / the market?**

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：That's stale dependency state, not a missing plugin file: the failing path will contain `node_modules/dsh-ntr/node_modules/.pnpm/...`. The source install uses `link:` to your checkout; pnpm's hoisted layout replaces the package directory with the registry files but leaves the link target's `node_modules` behind. That old tree (an older `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` plus its broken `zod` symlink) shadows the freshly installed dependency, so DSH's import hits the bad link and fails with `EPERM`. Fix: uninstall `dsh-ntr` in the plugin manager, remove `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-ntr` (or just its nested `node_modules`), then reinstall and restart. For the desktop app's profile, uninstall/reinstall from the app's Plugins page instead of the CLI.

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：**An NTR session shows `Error: unknown tool "xxx"` followed by a "Tool added: xxx" line. What is that?**

Display-layer noise from the host's card execution record. It is not a failed tool call in the agent.

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：In an NTR session the agent's tools run inside its own process, and the host only receives notifications. The host still executes each card once, because that execution record is what draws the card. The host has no definition for that name, so the guard registers a virtual tool at execution time and answers with the output the bridge recorded.

dsh-ntr README · FAQ：But the step's executable tool set is fixed before the request goes out. A tool registered during execution cannot join that step. So the first call of that tool name records `unknown tool`, and the next request assembly sees one extra tool and writes the "Tool added" line.

Impact: this happens once per tool name per session. The turn is not interrupted and the agent is unaffected. That card shows no mirrored output; the real output is in the NTR tab.

dsh-ntr README · What it can do (feature list)：- **Any ACP agent**: common presets built in, and any stdio-capable ACP agent works. Custom agents carry a "Custom" badge.
- **Multi-conversation isolation**: several conversations can talk to different agents at the same time, fully independent.
- **Streaming everything**: user messages, agent replies, thinking, tool execution, and task plans are all streamed.
- **Inlined tool activity**: tool calls are inserted into the main chat in the order they happened, with thinking and replies on either side — no layering.
- **Real permissions**: the agent's permission modes are listed verbatim, and every permission request is presented as-is. What you answer is what it receives.
- **Slash commands belong to the agent**: in NTR conversations, `/` pops the agent's own declared commands; DSH's same-named commands don't hijack your input.
- **Reconnect**: after a browser refresh or a network drop, history backfills in order. If the agent process crashed, the next message recovers it when the agent declares `session/load`.
- **Idle release**: agent processes with no activity exit automatically after an idle window, freeing memory; idle conversation

dsh-ntr README · Minimal config：Optional agent fields: `npmPackage` (auto `npm install -g` when not found on PATH), `exposedModels` (which variants the NTR seat menu lists), `idleTimeoutMs` (idle-release window for chat processes; `0` = never release, default 30 minutes), `mcpServers` (extra MCP servers handed to the agent). Reliability timeouts and retries (`startupTimeoutMs`, `cancelFallbackMs`, `staleCancelRetryDelayMs`, `staleCancelMaxRetries`, `permissionTimeoutMs`, `permissionTimeoutMode`, plus the stall watchdog's `turnStallMs` / `turnStallToolMs` / `turnStallTickMs`) are covered by [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) constraints 12, 13 and 23; anything editable in the Settings page should be edited there — the three watchdog keys live in the config file only (`turnStallMs: 0` disables the whole watchdog).

dsh-ntr README · Minimal config：These servers are handed to the agent when a session is created; the agent launches and uses them itself. The MCP servers the agent configures for itself are unaffected — this only adds more.

dsh-ntr README · Implementation notes：- **DSH renders, nothing more**: the plugin doesn't write DSH's model routing, doesn't take over the host's model catalog, and never lets ACP models appear in DSH's native selector.
- **Workspace = the side-panel path**: the directory opened in the side panel must become both the `session/new` cwd **and** the agent child's own cwd. One agent (codebuddy) pins its workspace at process startup.
- **NTR mode = an agent preset**: declared by `presets/acp/acp.patch.yml` shipped with the package — no tools, no injected project instructions, no compaction, so everything the model sees belongs to the remote agent.
- **Forwarding is strictly the user's text**: messages are picked by `source.kind === 'user'`; title generation, compaction, and other auxiliary calls aren't forwarded, and no boundary narration is ever spliced in.
